theme: Covenant renewed; the secret things belong to God
readingInstruction: Read Deuteronomy 29:1-31:29. In this reading, Moses calls Israel to renew the covenant, gives the famous “secret things” verse, and then hands over leadership to Joshua. Notice the call to choose life.
settingTheScene: After the blessings and curses, Moses gathers the people for a covenant renewal ceremony in the land of Moab. Chapter 29 describes the covenant, with a warning against secret idolatry and a prophecy of exile. Chapter 30 gives a promise of restoration, a call to choose life, and the statement that God’s word is near. Chapter 31 deals with the transfer of leadership to Joshua, the writing of the law, and the foretelling of Israel’s future rebellion.
observation: “You have seen all that the LORD did before your eyes in the land of Egypt… But to this day the LORD has not given you a heart to understand or eyes to see or ears to hear” (29:2-4).
“It is not with you alone that I am making this sworn covenant, but with whoever is standing here with us today… and with whoever is not here with us today” (29:14-15).
“The secret things belong to the LORD our God, but the things that are revealed belong to us and to our children forever, that we may do all the words of this law” (29:29).
“When all these things come upon you… and you return to the LORD your God… then the LORD your God will restore your fortunes and have compassion on you” (30:1-3).
“The LORD your God will circumcise your heart and the heart of your offspring, so that you will love the LORD your God with all your heart” (30:6).
“For this commandment that I command you today is not too hard for you, neither is it far off” (30:11).
“I have set before you life and death, blessing and curse. Therefore choose life, that you and your offspring may live” (30:19).
Moses commissions Joshua: “Be strong and courageous… It is the LORD who goes before you. He will be with you; he will not leave you or forsake you” (31:6-8).
interpretation:
Chapter 29 begins with a startling observation: after all the miracles, Israel still lacks a heart to understand. Moses says that God had not given them “a heart to understand or eyes to see or ears to hear.” It is a surprising admission. Seeing miracles does not change the heart. Only God can do that. And this is exactly what chapter 30 promises: “The LORD your God will circumcise your heart.” The problem of the heart is solved by God’s own gift.

The “secret things” verse is a great statement about knowing and not knowing. There are things God has not told us, and we should not be anxious about them. And there are things he has revealed, which belong to us, so that we may obey. The secret things are God’s business. The revealed things are ours. It frees us from speculation and calls us to obedience.

Chapter 30 is the hope of the book. Even after the curses fall, even after exile, there is a way back. “When you return to the LORD your God… he will gather you.” Repentance is always possible. And the way is not impossible: “The word is very near you. It is in your mouth and in your heart, so that you can do it.” God’s call is not a distant puzzle. It is close at hand.

Then comes the choice. “I have set before you life and death, blessing and curse. Therefore choose life.” Moses puts the whole book into one sentence. The people are not forced. They are invited. And choosing life is described as “loving the LORD your God, obeying his voice, and holding fast to him.”

Chapter 31 turns to the future. Moses commissions Joshua and tells him not to be afraid. He writes the law down and places it beside the ark. And he tells the people that after his death they will become corrupt. The tone is realistic. God knows that they will fail. He gives a song, which you will read tomorrow, to be a witness against them.
connection: Paul quotes Deuteronomy 30:11-14 in Romans 10:6-8 and applies it to the gospel: “The word is near you, in your mouth and in your heart (that is, the word of faith that we proclaim).” He says that Christ is the end of the law for righteousness to everyone who believes (Romans 10:4). Paul says that circumcision is of the heart (Romans 2:29), and Jesus said, “I came that they may have life and have it abundantly” (John 10:10). Hebrews 13:5 quotes 31:6: “I will never leave you nor forsake you.”
application:
Make a list of “secret things” that trouble you. Give them to God, and act on what is revealed.

Choose life today in one specific decision.

Take courage from God’s promise to Joshua. Receive it as spoken to you.
prayerPrompts: Give God the secret things you do not understand.
Ask him to circumcise your heart so that you love him.
Thank him that he goes before you and will not leave you.
